question.text: What is the minimum Capital to Risk-weighted Assets Ratio (CRAR) required for an AD Category-I bank to become a Trading and Clearing Member of the Currency Derivatives Segment?

explanation.text: The Logic: Per pages 199 and 206, the workbook lists a minimum CRAR of 10 per cent as one of the prudential requirements for an AD Category-I bank to become a trading and clearing member of the currency derivatives segment. The Trap: 12 per cent and 15 per cent are higher distractor thresholds, not the workbook minimum. Note: The same workbook section pairs the 10 per cent CRAR with net worth of at least Rs. 500 crores, net NPA not exceeding 3 per cent, and net profit for the last 3 years.
